newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares close firm in technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares close firm in technical rebound.

text.p: Snapping a string of losing sessions, Chilean blue chips rebounded to close sharply higher helped by Wall Street's surge and a technical rally after recent losses, said traders.
But light turnover means that the rally is likely to peter out at Tuesday's opening with the market's underlying mood remaining weak, they said.
"The poor volume means there is no real buying power," said one dealer.
The 40-share IPSA index ended up 1.11 percent at 90.55 points.
The general IGPA index ended up 0.33 percent at 4,989.78 points.
Turnover was a thin 7.8 billion pesos.

Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts closed firm with surges in electricity stocks which have fallen steeply recently as a result of a scare over the impact of this year's drought on company earnings, said dealers.
Endesa jumped 2.38 percent to 16-1/8 with Enersis climbing 1.9 percent to 26-7/8.
Despite Monday's rally, blue chip stocks could hit resistence at 91 points, said traders.

The low prices have tempted local institutional investors to bargain-hunt selectively but the market's volatility and high local interest rates mean they are unlikely to return to the bourse with any force in the near future, they said.
Winners included pulp producer Copec, up 1.61 percent at 1,580 pesos, fertilizer producer Soquimich, up 1.36 percent at 2,230 pesos and winery Concha y Toro which rose 1.06 percent to 189 pesos.
Losers included brewery CCU, down 3.55 percent at 1,495 pesos, forestry firm Masisa, down 0.55 percent at 182 pesos and copper products maker Madeco which shed 0.52 percent to 960 pesos.
